about: Inputs for /allotments.html. Scenario parameters are illustrative assumptions, not any airline's figures. The context timeline quotes public index headlines; each entry links to its source. Compiled 2026-09-30.

lane.season: July to December, weeks 1 to 26; the peak is centred on week 20 (mid-November)

scenarios.name: Base case
scenarios.blurb: A normal year: spot rates average a little above the contract rate, move about 6% a week, and rise into a November peak.

scenarios.name: Very volatile (2020–21)
scenarios.blurb: Belly capacity disappears and rates jump in steps that last for weeks, mostly upwards. Contracts were signed before the jump, at the old rate.

scenarios.name: Soft market
scenarios.blurb: Too much capacity chasing cargo: spot rates sit below the contract rate, demand is thin and forwarders ship part of their allotted cargo on the cheaper spot market.

scenarios.name: Strong peak season
scenarios.blurb: The base case with a much stronger October–December peak, as in e-commerce and new-product launch years: spot rates up 50% and demand up 45% at the top.

scenarios.name: No-show penalty
scenarios.blurb: The base case, but the contract makes forwarders pay half the contract rate on committed space they don't use, beyond a 10% tolerance.

context.label: April 2020
context.headline: Shanghai–North America $6.95/kg, up 131% since 1 March
context.text: Passenger flights were grounded and their belly capacity went with them. The TAC Index for Shanghai–North America reached $6.95/kg on 17 April 2020, a record since the index started in 2016; Shanghai–Europe was $8.65/kg, up 273% in six weeks. A week later Shanghai–North America was $7.59/kg, and one-off charters from China were quoted at $14–16/kg.

sources.name: TAC Index via Cargo News Wire, 17 Apr 2020

context.label: December 2021
context.headline: Rates almost 150% above December 2019
context.text: IATA reported record air cargo rates at the end of 2021, almost 150% above December 2019. Belly capacity was still 39% below 2019 (January–November) while freighter capacity was up 26%, and the international cargo load factor hit an all-time high of 63.9%.

sources.name: IATA Air Cargo Market Analysis, December 2021 (published 25 Jan 2022)

context.label: December 2023
context.headline: Hong Kong–North America peaks at $7.10/kg, then the index drops 20.5% in two weeks
context.text: The Baltic Air Freight Index (TAC data) had Hong Kong–North America at $7.10/kg in December 2023, up from $6.15 in November and 9.2% above December 2022. The overall index then fell 20.5% in the two weeks to 1 January 2024, and the lane ended the month below $6.

context.label: May 2025
context.headline: China–North America $5.28/kg as US de minimis rules change
context.text: The Freightos Air Index put China–North America at $5.28/kg, China–North Europe at $3.49/kg and North Europe–North America at $1.91/kg in early May 2025, each down 5–6% on the week as the US ended duty-free de minimis entry for Chinese e-commerce parcels.

context.label: December 2025
context.headline: Hong Kong–North America $6.60/kg, the high of the year
context.text: December 2025 averaged $6.60/kg from Hong Kong to North America and $5.44/kg to Europe, the highest months of 2025, but still 1.9% and 0.9% below December 2024. The transpacific had run as much as 13% behind the year before in June.

context.label: March 2026
context.headline: Middle East conflict: the index jumps 9.3% in a week
context.text: With conflict in the Middle East disrupting capacity and jet fuel about double its level a year earlier, the Baltic Air Freight Index rose 9.3% in the week to 30 March 2026. Hong Kong–North America was about $5.70/kg and Hong Kong–Europe $5.45/kg, heading back towards the $6.79 and $5.71 of the previous peak season in what is normally a quiet month.

context.label: August 2026
context.headline: Global index +18% year on year, jet fuel +74%
context.text: The Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI00) was flat through August 2026 but 18.1% above a year earlier, with China–US up 28.7%. Hong Kong–US West Coast spot rates were HK$45.62/kg (about US$5.85) at the end of August. Jet fuel averaged 74% more than a year before, and ocean shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was still disrupted.

indices.name: Baltic Air Freight Index (BAI), calculated by TAC Index
